t: Korea's longest-ruling dynasty, founded by Yi Seong-gye in 1392 and ruled from Hanseong, today's Seoul.
A model Neo-Confucian state run by examination-trained yangban officials; King Sejong created the Korean alphabet in 1443.
It survived Japanese and Manchu invasions but was forced open by Japan in 1876 and became the Korean Empire in 1897.
dyk: The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty record 472 years of government day by day, written by court historians whose drafts even the king was not supposed to read.
ev: Yi Seong-gye deposes the last Goryeo king and founds Joseon
King Sejong creates the Korean alphabet
The Gyeongguk daejeon law code is promulgated
Hideyoshi invades; Yi Sun-sin wins at Hansan Island
Injo surrenders to the Qing after the siege of Namhansanseong
The Treaty of Ganghwa opens Korea to Japan
